app.title: RobustPrint Virtual Lab
app.summary: A person sets the input material's distribution (the mean fraction of each component, how consistent batches are, and moisture) and a set of process settings on a ticket that every step shares. A bench view shows the simulated outcome for the average batch and for many random batches. The person then runs a simulated campaign or imports and validates their own CSV of runs, and trains a surrogate model for strength plus a print-success classifier, scored on held-out batches. Next, they optimise settings under several risk objectives, deploy them on fresh batches and compare the results. Finally they propose the next runs, either printing them in the simulator and retraining or copying them out as a CSV template.

task.text: Choose process settings that hold up across a variable input material, and plan the most informative next experiments, using a surrogate model trained on past runs.

data.text: A table of experimental runs, one row per job. Each row holds the input's measured composition (fractions that sum to one), its moisture, eight process settings, whether the job succeeded, and the mean and SD of the measured strength over replicate specimens. The input material is also described as a Dirichlet distribution over composition.
data.item: a print job: one feedstock batch printed at one set of process settings, with its replicate strength measurements and success flag

stage.text: modelling a run campaign to pick robust process settings and plan the next round of experiments

mechanism.text: A shared sidebar ticket holds the input distribution and the process settings, and every step reads it. Steps numbered along a top bar move from generating or importing data, to training and scoring a model, to optimising and deploying settings, to proposing the next runs. A 'Use' button on a recommendation writes its settings back to the ticket and opens the bench.

field.text: uncertainty-aware process optimisation and active learning for fused-filament 3D printing of recycled feedstock

workflow.name: fit a model to experimental runs, choose robust settings, and plan the next runs

steps.step: describe the input's variability and the settings to try
steps.here: Sliders on the job ticket set each component's mean fraction (the others rescale to keep the sum at one), a Dirichlet concentration for batch-to-batch consistency, median moisture and eight print settings. A stream preset loads a nominal or a shifted feedstock.

steps.step: look at the outcome across many draws of the input
steps.here: The bench shows strength, modulus, clogging and warping risk for the average batch, a waterfall of where strength is lost, a strip of the next batches drawn from the stream, and response curves for one chosen setting with 5–95 % bands across batches.
Run a simulated campaign (batches × settings × specimens over a Latin hypercube), or choose or paste a CSV and press Validate, which lists errors and warnings row by row, before 'Use N valid jobs'.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Train model' fits a physics-residual Gaussian process for log strength and a boosted-tree success classifier. It is disabled until there are 5 jobs with a strength. The model is scored on held-out batches with RMSE, CRPS, 90 % coverage and Brier score, plus parity and calibration plots and input relevance.

Tick the objectives to run (nominal, expected, 5 % quantile, CVaR, chance-constrained) and decide with the learned model, the hidden truth, or both. 'Optimise and deploy' prints each recommendation on fresh batches and compares failure rate, expected utility and strength distributions.

steps.step: propose the next runs and iterate
steps.here: Choose an acquisition strategy and a number of jobs, then 'Propose experiments'. 'Print them and retrain' appends the simulated results and refits, and a regret chart tracks the true quality of each round's recommendation.
'Copy CSV' exports the campaign, and 'Copy as a CSV template' writes the proposed jobs in the import schema, ready to fill in after printing.

distinctive: The input is a probability distribution over a composition simplex rather than a fixed value, so settings are chosen for the next, uncharacterised batch.
Risk objectives (quantile, CVaR, chance constraint) are compared with a nominal objective under a minimum print-success constraint.
A hidden ground-truth simulator lets the person reveal true values and score recommendations by regret. With imported real data, scoring is turned off and only model predictions are shown.
Each recommendation reports what share of its predictive variance comes from the feedstock rather than from the model or noise.
Proposed experiments carry a cost (setup plus relative print time), and a cost-aware strategy can be chosen.
